unlocks.stayRule: The St. Maarten Tourist Bureau gives a standard uninterrupted tourist stay of 30 days. Nationals of Canada, the European Union other than the Netherlands, Australia, New Zealand and Japan may stay for three uninterrupted months; Dutch and US nationals may stay for six uninterrupted months. Longer stays follow the applicable extension procedure. The period authorized at the border controls the visit.
unlocks.notes: The residence permit supplies the visa exemption. The local nationality-based table supplies the admission periods; the general 90-days-in-180 statement on NetherlandsWorldwide is recorded separately.

unlocks.conditions: Valid US residence permit exempts the holder from a Caribbean visa.
unlocks.additionalRequirements: Passport issued within ten years and valid throughout the stay; proof of return eligibility, purpose and accommodation; funds (hotel USD 150–200/person/day; family USD 100/person/day or sponsorship); medical coverage at least USD 15,000 including hospital care, emergency care and repatriation. Local authority may admit for a shorter period; work requires a permit. For Bonaire, the Visitor Entry Tax is normally USD 75; children aged 12 or younger, qualifying island children and residents of the other five former-Antilles islands qualify for USD 10, with proof. Bonaire residents and qualifying students are exempt; cruise passengers have a separate USD 10 levy paid through the cruise line. Arrange the tax QR code before arrival; the published kiosk option permits payment on arrival if online payment fails. These Bonaire tax rules concern Bonaire, while the BQ code also covers Saba and Sint Eustatius.
